ut_black_rocks_boulders.blurb: A bouldering-only pocket of basalt blocks scattered along the desert wash that runs through the Black Rocks crag outside St. George, around 3,200 feet. Two dozen problems run from VB up to V8, with the bulk in the V2 to V5 range and a thin tail of harder lines above that. The stone is dark, slick and sharp-edged, with pockets and low friction, so skin takes a beating. Unlike the sandstone at nearby Moe's, the basalt can be climbed soon after rain. It sits right between the sunny and shady sides of the roped crag, which makes it easy to combine with a day of sport climbing.

ut_banshee_wall.blurb: One of the cliffs on the south side of the Jungle, a high-elevation volcanic-rock crag near 10,400 feet on the Aquarius Plateau in south-central Utah. The wall holds about two dozen routes, a roughly even split of trad and sport, with grades from 5.6 to 5.12 and the heaviest concentration at 5.10. Lines are steep and technical, following arete and edge features, and the rock is generally solid though welded tuff can be loose in places. It is a drive-up alpine setting, with a short walk through forest from the road, a stretch of cairned trail and a steep descent to the base.

ut_s_curve_lower.blurb: The largest wall at the S-Curves in Big Cottonwood Canyon, in the central Wasatch east of Salt Lake City. About two dozen routes, mostly bolted sport lines plus a handful of trad lines, climb steep to overhanging quartzite that is hard and slippery yet covered in holds at all angles. Grades start in the easy 5.6 to 5.8 range and reach into the 5.13s and 5.14, though most routes cluster around 5.11. The base is a short walk from the road, and the east end has some trees for shade. A good pick for steep, powerful sport climbing close to town.

ut_tee_pee_boulder.blurb: The main boulder cluster of the Tee Pee area in Moe's Valley, a sandstone bouldering destination near St. George in the far southwest corner of Utah. About two dozen problems span the whole range, from VB to V10, with a good number of easy and moderate lines in the V1 to V4 band and a respectable set of hard ones from V8 up. The sandstone is soft and can be fragile, so treat holds gently. It is reached on foot from the road end in a short valley hike, and it is one of the more popular clusters in the valley, a natural winter destination.
